- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.27) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward with more aggressive slope.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast horizon) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias to compensate for lag.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is consolidating, model often overpredicts volatility; smooth forecast curve to reflect reduced momentum.
- For long-term horizon (e.g., 30-day), model frequently overestimates final price; apply downward bias of 1–2% to align with historical mean reversion patterns.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a “cooling” factor to prevent runaway forecasts.
